narration: We start from a pre-trained 3D Gaussian Splatting model with frozen parameters.
Frequency Guided Densification decides where the scene needs more Gaussians.
The result is the densified model G-o-prime, ready for fine-tuning.
Inside FGD, Phase 1 ranks every Gaussian by its contribution to rendering quality.
The lowest-contributing Gaussians are removed from the cloud.
Phase 2 begins by rendering the scene from several viewpoints.
Each rendered view is patchified into a regular grid of patches.
A Discrete Fourier Transform maps every patch into frequency space.
Each spectrum is multiplied by a quadratic mask to detect high frequency energy.
The patches with the strongest high-frequency response are selected.
Gaussians covering those regions are split, adding capacity for fine detail.
Back in the main pipeline, a gradient mask chooses which attributes may change.
Applying it gives the fine-tuned, unfrozen watermarked model G-w.
Rendering that model produces the watermarked image.
A Discrete Wavelet Transform separates the render by frequency.
This yields a low-frequency band and the high-frequency details.
The frozen pre-trained decoder reads the low-frequency band.
It outputs the decoded message hidden in the rendering.
The ground-truth view passes through the same wavelet transform for comparison.
Three losses compare the image, the wavelet bands, and the message.
They are summed into the total loss.
The optimizer back-propagates it through the mask, updating the Gaussians.
